packages/matter/src/controller.ts.content: `commands` returns the internal `recorded` array by reference. The `readonly` modifier is a compile-time annotation only — at runtime any caller (tests, simulator, future adapters) can `push`/`pop`/`splice`/`length = 0` on it and silently corrupt the ordered command log that assertions depend on. Return a shallow copy so the adapter owns its history.

Lifecycle after `close()` is inconsistent. `close()` only flips `closed` and leaves every commissioned node in `nodes`, while `commission`/`command`/`read` throw `MatterError("stopped")` — yet the inspection helpers `nodeState()` (and `commands`) skip the guard entirely. A stopped controller therefore still reports full node state and command history, which can make "refuses all work after close" assertions pass while stale data leaks. Either clear `nodes` on close and guard `nodeState` consistently, or document explicitly that these are post-close-readable inspection helpers.

`not-confirmed` and `already-bound` are declared in `MatterReason` but are never produced by any code path — `commission` never checks whether a node/pairing is already bound, and there is no confirmation step. Consumers may write handling branches for reasons that can never fire. Either implement the duplicate-binding/confirmation checks or remove the dead reasons.

packages/rekordbox-library/src/anlz.ts.content: `swapSuffix` only recognizes `/` as the path separator. `join()` (and the stored absolute fallback) produce platform-native paths, so on Windows `slash` is always -1 and the `dot <= slash` guard becomes inert. In that case any dot that is not the file extension — e.g. a dotted directory segment in `/share/PIONEER/v1.2/ANLZ0000` — is treated as the extension and the sliced path becomes corrupted, yielding wrong `.EXT`/`.2EX` paths and therefore wrong `anlz-partial`/`anlz-ok` statuses. Using the `node:path` helpers removes the separator assumption.

This swallows every errno as "not found". Permission/resource errors (EACCES, EMFILE, EIO, ENOTDIR) are indistinguishable from ENOENT, so they are silently reported as `anlz-missing` / `anlz-partial` and the caller cannot tell a genuinely absent file from an unreadable one. Since a missing file is already modeled as a status, non-ENOENT errors should be surfaced (rethrow or return a distinct signal) rather than converted to a missing status. Note this also does not verify the path is a regular file, so a directory at `datPath`/`audioPath` is reported as existing.

Two concerns with this expression: (1) it stats `joined` (and possibly `stored`) to make the decision, then `facts(datPath, statFile)` re-stats the chosen path, so the DAT is stat'ed twice per row and the decision is based on a snapshot that can differ from the recorded facts (TOCTOU). Prefer resolving the path once and reusing the stat result. (2) `isAbsolute(stored)` is true on POSIX for the documented normal case (stored paths carry a leading `/` but are share-relative), so the absolute-wins fallback probes the filesystem root (`/PIONEER/...`) whenever the share-relative file is absent; the intended fallback should be triggered by an actually absolute stored path, not by the leading-separator convention.

packages/rekordbox-library/src/readonly..content: The INSERT and DROP probes only assert `rejected === true`. `attemptWrite()` returns `rejected: true` for ANY thrown error (driver.ts), so an unrelated failure — a syntax/schema mismatch, a missing table, or a non-read-only driver error — would satisfy this assertion without proving the database actually blocked the write. Assert the error matches the read-only reason here as well (`expect(direct.error).toMatch(/readonly|read-only|query_only/i)`).

Unlike the other cases in this file, this test does not wrap the probe in `try/finally`: if `probeWrite()` rejects or the assertions fail, `reader.close()` is skipped. It is currently harmless because `SidecarReader.close()` is a no-op, but it is inconsistent with the surrounding tests and becomes a real leak if the reader later holds a process/handle. Wrap the probe and assertions in `try { ... } finally { reader.close(); }`.

The write-method detection only inspects own prototype property names against a fixed list, so write-shaped methods with names outside the list (e.g. `set`, `put`, `mutate`, `saveAll`, `insertMany`) would slip through; `Object.getOwnPropertyNames` also excludes Symbol-keyed methods, and the getters `mode`/`reader` plus instance own-properties are never checked. Consider walking the full prototype chain, checking own-property names/symbols, and asserting an explicit allowlist of read-only operations rather than a deny-list.
